The base of the EGRADX server SDK for Node; the counterpart of the Java `egradx-core`.

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `AuthenticationException`, `AuthorizationException`, `NotFoundException`, `DuplicateResourceException`, `ValidationException` / `BadRequestException`, `EgradxInternalException`, base `EgradxError` | The Java SDK's exception names. Each maps to the contract's status and generic code (401 `NOT_AUTHENTICATED`, 403 `ACCESS_DENIED`, 404 `NOT_FOUND`, 409 `CONFLICT`, 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`). An optional second argument gives a more specific code. |
| `errorBody(code, message, requestId, details?)` | The error envelope of `contracts/schemas/error.json`. |
| `runWithContext`, `currentContext`, `currentRequestId`, `logFields` | The per-request context (`AsyncLocalStorage`): request id, locale, user agent, the signed-in caller. Framework adapters create it. |
| `acceptableRequestId`, `newRequestId` | The request-id rule shared with Java: 1–64 of `A-Za-z0-9._-`. |
| Error-code constants and types, and the shared enums (`UserType`, …) | Generated from `contracts/schemas/` (`pnpm run generate`; the output is committed). |
| `EgradxAuditEvent.of(action)…build()`, `EgradxAuditActor`, `publishAuditEvent`, `registerAuditActions` | How any library records audit events without depending on `@babulvaibhav/egradx-audit`, as Java libraries publish Spring events. The builder uses the Java builder's method names. |
| `egradxTransaction(prisma, fn)`, `currentTransaction()` | A Prisma transaction that every EGRADX library joins without being passed it, and whose `afterCommit` callbacks run only once it commits. An audit record commits with the change; a notification is pushed, or its delivery started, only after the commit. |
| `formatInstant`, `sqlMicros`, `microsOf`, `uuidV7`, `isUuid` | Times read with PostgreSQL's microsecond precision and written as Java's `Instant.toString()` writes them. A JavaScript `Date` (and Prisma's pg adapter, which drops the session's offset when it reads one) would lose that. |
| `ServerAuthenticationException` (401), `ServerAuthorizationException` (403), `NotImplementedException` (501), `ServerUnavailableException` (503), `ServerException(status)` | Java's errors of calling another service, with the contract's statuses and generic codes; every 5xx is `INTERNAL_ERROR`, its message never sent. |
| `sealSecretText(plaintext, passphrase)`, `openSecretText(sealed, passphrase)` | Java's `EncryptionUtil.sealText`/`openText`: the envelope below as one string, `v1:<kekSalt>:<encryptedDek>:<ciphertext>`. The replacement for Java's deprecated DES `CommonUtils.encrypt`. |
| `generateRandomString(length)`, `getZippedContent(text)`, `getUnzippedContent(bytes)` | Java's `RandomStringGeneratorUtil` and `CommonUtils`: letters and digits from `crypto.randomInt`; UTF-8 gzip that either SDK reads (`contracts/test-vectors/core-utils.json`). |
| `ControlManager`, `Control` | Java's `ControlManager`: components started, in the order registered, when the application calls `start()`, and stopped by `stop()`. A failure to start fails the startup; a failure to stop is logged. |
| `applicationProperties(env?)` | Java's `egradx.app.*` (`softwareId`, `softwareName`, `softwareVersion`, `softwareRepositoryName`), from the variables Spring Boot binds: `EGRADX_APP_SOFTWAREID` and so on. |
| `sealSecret(plaintext, passphrase)`, `openSecret(envelope, passphrase)` | Java's `EncryptionUtil` envelope encryption, byte for byte. Each SDK opens what the other sealed: AES-256-GCM, with the data key wrapped under a PBKDF2-SHA256 key (210,000 iterations). |

### ControlManager

Starts every registered Control when the application is ready, and stops them when it shuts down, each in the order
registered. As Java's ControlManager, which does so on Spring's context refreshed and closed events: here the
application calls `start()` once it is ready and `stop()` on shutdown. A control that fails to start fails the
startup, and those after it are not started; one that fails to stop is logged, and the rest still stop.

### EgradxAuditEvent

Something worth an audit record: who did what, to what, with what result. Actions are named
`category.entity.verb`, lower case with underscores (`auth.password.changed`). Every value is checked
when the event is built, so a malformed event fails where it is written, not inside a transaction.
`before`, `after` and `details` are stored as JSON; secrets are redacted by key, but should not be passed.

### EgradxError

An error the SDK turns into the error envelope (contracts/schemas/error.json) with this status and
code. Throw one of the subclasses below from anywhere in a request; the framework adapter's error

### PrismaLike

### SecretEnvelope

the application's passphrase encrypts that. All three fields are Base64, all three must be stored, and
none is sensitive without the passphrase.

```ts

```

USER: signed in. ANONYMOUS: not signed in. SYSTEM: the application itself. UNKNOWN: in a request, but nothing said by whom.

***

### EgradxAuditDurability

```ts
type EgradxAuditDurability = "WITH_TRANSACTION" | "INDEPENDENT";
```

Whether a record shares the fate of the transaction it was made in. Unset: a SUCCESS is
WITH_TRANSACTION (commits with the change, or not at all) and anything else INDEPENDENT (stored at
once, surviving the caller's rollback).

How the audited attempt ended.

### openSecret()

```ts
function openSecret(envelope, passphrase): Promise<string>;
```

Reverses [sealSecret](#sealsecret), and opens what Java's EncryptionUtil.seal produced.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `envelope` | [`SecretEnvelope`](#secretenvelope) |
| `passphrase` | `string` |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`string`\>

#### Throws

Error if the passphrase is wrong or any part has been altered; GCM cannot tell those apart

***

### openSecretText()

```ts
function openSecretText(sealed, passphrase): Promise<string>;
```

Reverses [sealSecretText](#sealsecrettext), and opens what Java's EncryptionUtil.sealText produced.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `sealed` | `string` |
| `passphrase` | `string` |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`string`\>

#### Throws

Error if `sealed` is not in the text form, and as [openSecret](#opensecret) if the passphrase is wrong or it was altered

### publishAuditEvent()

```ts
function publishAuditEvent(event, options?): Promise<void>;
```

Publishes an audit event, as a Java library publishes one as a Spring event: @babulvaibhav/egradx-audit stores it
when the application uses it; without it the event goes nowhere. Pass the transaction the change is
made in, so a success commits with it.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `event` | [`EgradxAuditEvent`](#egradxauditevent) |
| `options` | [`EgradxAuditPublishOptions`](#egradxauditpublishoptions) |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`void`\>

***

### sealSecret()

```ts
function sealSecret(plaintext, passphrase): Promise<SecretEnvelope>;
```

Encrypts `plaintext` under a fresh data key, wrapped under a key derived from `passphrase`.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `plaintext` | `string` |
| `passphrase` | `string` |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<[`SecretEnvelope`](#secretenvelope)\>

***

### sealSecretText()

```ts
function sealSecretText(plaintext, passphrase): Promise<string>;
```

[sealSecret](#sealsecret), as one string for one text column: `v1:<kekSalt>:<encryptedDek>:<ciphertext>`, each part Base64.
Java's EncryptionUtil.sealText, the replacement for its deprecated DES CommonUtils.encrypt; every SDK writes and reads
it alike (contracts/test-vectors/secret-envelope.json).

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `plaintext` | `string` |
| `passphrase` | `string` |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`string`\>
